verdicts.reason: A keeps the original's centred stack and hierarchy, but it reads as a shrunk copy. The wordmark now sits on the teal circle, the content crowds the upper two-thirds, and the tiny legal line floats over a dead band at the bottom. B overscales the product, which dominates the canvas. It jams the headline against the bottom-left edge and shrinks the CTA into a small pill in the bottom-right corner, where it is buried. The legal text is squeezed into an illegible four-line wrap under the CTA, so hierarchy and spacing are broken.
